topic: Keep rgv_long + capitulation_long — router as their guard
play: KEEP the two long-faders (rgv_long, capitulation_long) live — do NOT relegate. Left naked they bleed; guarded by the direction-router they are a chop specialist. The router already benched them correctly on every proven down-leg this week, with zero leaks.

Unfiltered proxies are ugly (capit_loose -$3,268, rg_long_fast -$1,650) but that is a ROUTING problem, not a filter one. Friday: 0 of 18 long-fader entries leaked through a bench window. capitulation_long was the ONLY live gate that didn't bleed this week (+$17). Keep + router guard beats relegate.

play: Do NOT blanket re-enable the rgv absorption-confirm layer (the live-then-removed arc). Treat it as REGIME-CONDITIONAL: it is the filter that closes the router's blind spot for choppy grinds-against-you, so re-enable it only when the router reads CHOP (where the router itself does nothing), and leave it off when a trend is proven (the router already handles that). Shadow-test the conditional wiring before it goes back live.
rationale: The router protects against PROVEN trends but has a blind spot for choppy grinds against you — that is exactly where rgv_short lost -$345 in 13 fires into a chop up-grind on Friday before the +$183 redemption when the tape aligned. Closing that blind spot is a FILTER job (absorption-confirm), not a router or relegation job. The open question the report poses: gate the confirm on router-reads-chop so it doesn't also clip the trend fires the router already covers. Exploratory — prove the conditional in shadow first.

topic: Direction-router architecture — KEEP the clunky poll
play: KEEP the direction-router exactly as shipped (15-min poll, 2-mark hysteresis, switch-file). All three 'more elegant' alternatives you named — per-tick in-code guard, event-driven flip, continuous in-tournament gate — were built and raced on this week's real trades and every one made LESS money. The only thing worth stealing is cosmetic: let the tournament call the router's current_regime() itself to kill the switch-file race and partial-bar drift at identical latency (hygiene only, never naive per-tick).
rationale: Five-plumbing race over 131 counter-trend fader trades: shipped router kept +$736 by benching just 23 trades (all losers, $32 of loss removed each); per-tick CONTINUOUS kept only +$341 (benched 54, scooping up green rgv_short); event-driven LOST -$125. The decomposition settles it: the reaction lag the elegant designs fix is worth only -$57 all week, but the stickiness they'd remove is worth -$452 (nine concentrated losers the poll holds a proven trend long enough to bench). The STEPxHOLD map confirms the whole fast-and-twitchy corner is a graveyard. The exact 15/2 cell is in-sample noise; the coarse-and-sticky direction is robust. Migrate for hygiene later; do not migrate behaviour.

play: DO NOT ARM any new run-catching entry. Ran three times over (full census, top-25, top-15 biggest runs). Every causal entry invented from a blank sheet — flow-continuation, volume-breakout, chase-the-flow, vacuum-fade, Donchian breakout — is a 48-52% coin-flip that bleeds after realistic cost. Narrowing to the biggest, cleanest footprints did not reveal a stronger tell.
rationale: The runs ARE real money and the exit is fine — the problem is purely the ENTRY: a real-time run-start is statistically indistinguishable from the chop-bursts around it. M2 already proved our own six gates, fired ungated in the run's direction in the 10 minutes before each of the 43 sat-out runs ($8,959 of hindsight money), could not catch them either — a clean, provable no. Durable negative lesson, no green light.

topic: Donchian as a DETECTOR (the one survivor)
play: SHADOW the 5-min Donchian breakout as a non-trading 'a run may be starting' LABEL only — feeding the regime/shadow router, never as a capital gate. This is the one thing that survived the greenfield null: a lousy entry but a great detector.
rationale: As a trade it bleeds (-$5,056 traded) but as a real-time flag it catches 48 of 49 runs. Zero capital, zero P&L claim; it may earn its keep as a signal the direction-router LISTENS to (does a run appear to be starting?), not a trade it takes. Observe-only.
